mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent passport or civil registry authority of each individual's jurisdiction of origin

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory pre-incorporation screening of the settlor, all foundation council members, protectors, beneficiaries, and any indirect owner against the United Nations Security Council Consolidated Sanctions List, OFAC SDN and 50% ownership sanctions lists, EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, Panamanian UAF alert lists, and Superintendencia de Bancos de Panamá risk registries. PEP status is determined on a risk-sensitive basis and triggers enhanced due diligence, senior-management approval, and ongoing monitoring. No person failing adverse-media or sanctions review may be named in the foundation charter.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registro Público de Panamá - Sistema de Reserva de Nombre en Línea / Sede Virtual del Registro Público
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: All corporate and foundation names must be submitted in Spanish or in an officially transliterated Spanish rendering. Names used outside Panama may be maintained in a secondary Latin-script or transliterated form, but the foundation's registered legal name must be capable of appearing in the Public Registry's Spanish index. The foundation name must end with 'Fundación de Interés Privado' or the accepted abbreviation 'F.I.P.'.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Write an administrative appeal to the Director General of the Registro Público de Panamá within ten business days of the refusal, accompanied by a new proposed name and payment of the corresponding search fee. If the refusal is based on a token reserved to a sectoral supervisor, the applicant must first obtain the applicable license, no-objection letter, or ministerial approval and then resubmit. Adverse registry decisions may be challenged through the administrative reconsideration and subsequent court review procedure pursuant to Panamanian registry administrative law.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Not permissible for the statutory seat. A Panamanian licensed resident agent maintaining a functioning physical office in the Republic of Panama is mandatory. Virtual office or mail-forwarding services may be used only for ancillary communication and cannot satisfy the registered-office requirement.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low for the passive foundation itself (estimated no-cause unannounced inspection probability under 5% per annum for this gaming IP holding scope), but moderate at the resident agent level (estimated 15-20% annual probability of review during UAF/Superintendencia AML audit cycles).

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Law No. 25 of 12 June 1995 (Private Interest Foundations), Articles 1-3 (creation and purpose), Article 10 (minimum initial capital), Articles 13-19 (Foundation Council and Protector), as amended by Law No. 8 of 2001; supplemental application of the Registro Público directives and Law No. 23 of 2015 (Anti-Money Laundering) regarding beneficial ownership disclosure.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registro Público de Panamá — Departamento de Fundaciones de Interés Privado, Mercantile Section, Sede Central, Panama City.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Acta Constitutiva (Foundation Charter), executed as a public deed before a Panamanian Notary Public and presented for electronic inscription in the Folio Electrónico of the Registro Público.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: USD 10,000.00 minimum initial endowment required under Article 10 of Law 25 of 1995. The endowment may consist of money, movable or immovable property, or rights of any kind, declared in the Foundation Charter. No mandatory escrow deposit or bank certification is required; the Founder's notarized declaration in the Charter is legally sufficient for registration. For the hyper-casual gaming asset-holding scope, a declared USD 10,000.00 endowment is compliant and may be increased later without registry amendment (additional contributions are recorded in the foundation's internal patrimony register).
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLUTION NO. 1 OF THE FOUNDATION COUNCIL OF [•] PRIVATE INTEREST FOUNDATION. The undersigned Foundation Council, acting under Law 25 of 12 June 1995, hereby resolves unanimously: (1) To accept the initial endowment of USD ten thousand (US$10,000) contributed by the Founder and to declare the Foundation's patrimony sufficient for its lawful statutory purposes. (2) To adopt the registered office of the Foundation at the office of the Founding Attorney in Panama City, Republic of Panama. (3) To appoint [President] and [Secretary-Treasurer] as members of the Foundation Council with joint-representation powers. (4) To authorize the Founding Attorney to file the Charter with the Public Registry of Panama, pay statutory fees, open bank accounts, and execute all ancillary instruments. Adopted unanimously in Panama City on [date].

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name Availability Verification and Foundation Name Reservation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Público de Panamá — Sede Electrónica (online certification portal) and Information Counter of the Mercantile Section.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The licensed Panamanian founding attorney submits three ranked proposed names (e.g., 'XYZ Hyper Games Foundation') through the Registry's online simple-certification service. The Registry verifies that no identical or confusingly similar name exists among registered foundations and mercantile companies. Upon approval, the attorney obtains the 'Certificado de No Objeción' reserving the selected name for thirty (30) calendar days.
required_dossiers: Written name-clearance request signed by the founding attorney
Three proposed foundation names in descending preference
Certified copy of the Founder's passport or Panama cédula
Attorney engagement letter / letter of instructions
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected as identical or confusingly similar, the attorney re-files with the alternative proposed names; a written clarification may be submitted to the Registry's technical staff. No monetary penalty applies; the 30-day reservation window resets upon the new certification.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting, Execution and Civil Notarization of the Foundation Charter
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notaría Pública del Circuito de Panamá (Notary Public of the Panama Judicial Circuit).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The founding attorney drafts the Acta Constitutiva in Spanish, including: the foundation's name and 'hyper-casual mobile game publishing and asset holding' purpose clause, registered office in Panama City, declaration of the initial endowment, designation of the Founder, beneficiary regime, optional Protector, and the composition of the Foundation Council. The Founder executes the deed personally or through an attorney-in-fact before the Notary, who authenticates the act and records the deed in the notarial protocol. The notarized 'primera copia' constitutes the executable title for registration.
required_dossiers: Draft Acta Constitutiva approved by the Founder
Optional Reglamento (internal regulations) if governance details are kept confidential
Name clearance certificate (Certificado de No Objeción)
Valid passport or cédula of the Founder and all Foundation Council members
Proof of payment of notarial fees (tariff arancel)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Notary issues a defect note, the attorney prepares a clarifying instrument (adenda) correcting the deficiency and re-executes it before the same Notary; the corrected deed is then re-submitted for registration without losing the original notarization priority date.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Electronic Inscription with the Public Registry of Panama (Private Interest Foundation Section)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Público de Panamá — Departamento de Fundaciones de Interés Privado, Mercantile Section.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within thirty (30) calendar days of notarization, the founding attorney submits the notarized first copy, the completed index card (carátula / hoja de inscripción), the beneficial ownership declaration, and the fee payment receipt through the 'Registro Electrónico' platform. The Registrar (Registrador) performs the qualification review (calificación). Upon approval, the foundation is inscribed with an asiento number in the Folio Electrónico, and the Registry issues the Certificate of Legal Existence (Certificado de Persona Jurídica / Fundación).
required_dossiers: Notarized first copy of the Acta Constitutiva
Name clearance certificate
Signed carátula / registration index card
Registro Público fee payment receipt (Banco Nacional de Panamá)
Beneficial ownership declaration under Law 23 of 2015
Power of attorney granted to the founding attorney (if applicable)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrador issues a 'defecto subsanable' (curable defect) notice, the attorney submits the clarifying document within ten (10) business days. If the defect is considered insubsanable, the attorney may reformulate the Charter and re-file (new fees apply) or appeal the decision before the Board of Directors of the Registro Público within fifteen (15) business days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Payment of Annual State Franchise Tax and Issuance of Official Receipt
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) — Ministry of Economy and Finance, through Banco Nacional de Panamá.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The founding attorney pays the fixed government franchise tax of USD 300.00 for private interest foundations into the State Treasury account at Banco Nacional de Panamá. Foundations incorporated after 30 June pay a pro-rated tax of USD 150.00 for the remainder of the calendar year. The stamped payment receipt is archived with the foundation's corporate register and demonstrates tax good standing before banks and counterparties.
required_dossiers: DGI tax payment form (Formulario de pago de impuesto de fundación)
Certified copy of the registered Foundation Charter
Registry inscription certificate (asiento)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Late payment accrues statutory surcharges and monthly interest under the Tax Code; the remedy is immediate payment of principal plus surcharge. If the foundation has been suspended or struck off for chronic non-payment, the attorney files a reinstatement request with DGI and the Registro Público accompanied by proof of full payment.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Registration Credentials, Apostille, and Ancillary Tax Registry (RUC) Filing
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Público de Panamá — Certification Office; Dirección General de Ingresos for RUC (optional).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Obtain certified copies of the registered Acta Constitutiva and the Certificate of Good Standing (Paz y Salvo fiscal y registral). For foreign bank onboarding, request apostille of the certified documents under the Hague Apostille Convention (competent authority: Dirección General de Registro Civil, or the Ministry of Foreign Affairs for apostille places, per national practice). If the foundation maintains a Panamanian bank account or institutional counterparty relationship, file the RUC application and complete the client due-diligence file under Law 23 of 2015. No operating license is required for the passive holding of gaming company shares.
required_dossiers: Certified copy of the inscribed Acta Constitutiva
Certificate of Good Standing (Paz y Salvo)
Apostille application form and fee receipt
Passports and residence proof of Founder and Council members
AML beneficial ownership statement (Law 23 of 2015)
RUC application form (Formulario de inscripción) if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If DGI identifies RUC data discrepancies, the attorney files a corrective amendment with the registry certificate attached. Apostille rejections are cured by re-certifying the notarial signature of the Registry certification officer and resubmitting; the DGI remedy carries no penalty if corrected within the administrative response term.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable to ISIC 5820 (publishing of lightweight ad-monetized mobile games). Reference authority for any incidental future physical establishment: Ministerio de Comercio e Industrias (MICI), Dirección General de Empresas y Actividades Industriales. The Private Interest Foundation is a passive asset-holding vehicle and performs no industrial or manufacturing activity.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: None required. Panamanian law imposes no sectoral license for digital software or hyper-casual game publishing (non-gambling content). If a physical administrative office is opened, a municipal 'Aviso de Operación' is procured from the Municipio de Panama; the PIF itself, being a holding entity with no local commercial operations, remains exempt.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministerio de Ambiente (MiAMBIENTE) — Dirección de Evaluación de Impacto Ambiental
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt from Full EIA (Cat. II/III not triggered). Software and game publishing generates no industrial emissions; a nominal Category I environmental notice (Aviso Ambiental) is required only if the entity establishes a physical office above 1,000 sqm or an on-premise server room; typical virtual operations are fully exempt.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No VOC, wastewater effluent, or hazardous process discharge is generated by hyper-casual game publishing. Incidental office operations must comply with the national public-health/plumbing code for sanitary wastewater (connection to municipal sewers, standard BOD/COD parameters per national water norms) and municipal solid-waste disposal rules; e-waste from replaced IT equipment must be handled by MiAMBIENTE-authorized recyclers. No industrial discharge permit is required.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification is required only if physical office premises are maintained, issued by the Cuerpo de Bomberos de Panama (inspection and operating certificate). Structural/load inspection and building-use clearance are obtained from the Municipio de Panama (Departamento de Obras y Construcciones). Occupational health clearance is issued by MITRADEL (Dirección de Higiene y Seguridad Industrial), and employer registration with the Caja de Seguro Social (CSS) is mandatory for any Panama-based employees; fully remote software development staff located abroad do not trigger these Panama obligations.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) of the Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas (MEF); official portal: Sede Electrónica DGI (https://dgi.mef.gob.pa) and PanamaTramita (panamatramita.gob.pa)
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign Private Interest Foundation (PIF) obtains its RUC (Registro Único de Contribuyente) by appointment at DGI through a resident legal representative. Submit notarized and apostilled foundation charter (Acta Constitutiva), evidence of registered address in Panama maintained by the foundation's resident agent under Ley 25 de 1995, and passport copies of foundation council members. DGI issues a provisional RUC on the spot; final RUC activates after domicile verification and, when local commercial activity exists, presentation of the municipal Aviso de Operación. PIFs with strictly foreign-source income may remain RUC-only, but must register for ITBMS to claim zero-rating and refunds.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Territorial_Scope - PIFs under Ley 25 de 1995 are not general ISR taxpayers on foreign-source income; only Panama-sourced income is subject to corporate ISR (25% standard rate); PIFs remain subject to the fixed annual PAB 300 State tax under Ley 25, Art. 20, payable through the resident agent.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box, CFC, or hybrid mismatch election exists in Panamanian tax law. Available elections: (i) simplified small taxpayer regime (régimen de pequeño contribuyente) where annual gross turnover ≤ PAB 36,000; (ii) election to register as a full ITBMS taxpayer to claim input credits and export refunds; (iii) charter-level election limiting the PIF to passive asset holding (tax-neutral) versus engaging in local trade (triggering full ISR/ITBMS exposure).

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: ITBMS - Impuesto de Transferencia de Bienes Muebles y Servicios (VAT-type transfer tax)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No general de minimis exemption - RUC and ITBMS registration are mandatory for any person performing taxable commercial acts in Panama; taxpayers with annual gross turnover ≤ PAB 36,000 may elect the simplified 'pequeño contribuyente' flat-rate regime instead of full periodic declaration.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory Facturación Electrónica under DGI Resolution 201-1886 and amendments: taxpayer must hold a digital signature certificate, operate a DGI-certified billing platform, and transmit each invoice in real time (online validation at issuance) to DGI's clearance system; each invoice carries a unique authorization code, XML/PDF with QR code, and DGI acknowledgement. Certified software vendors integrate via DGI REST API; unvalidated invoices are legally invalid and non-deductible.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of goods and services carry the 0% ITBMS rate under Ley 8 de 2010 when (i) goods physically leave Panamanian customs territory, or (ii) services are rendered to a non-resident for exclusive use and economic exploitation outside Panama. Hyper-casual game ad-monetization services provided to AdMob/AppLovin qualify as zero-rated exports because the platform counterparty is non-resident and end-users consume content abroad. The PIF must retain platform payout statements and a digital services supply contract; registration with DGI is required to validate the 0% rate and access input-credit refunds.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Declaración de Exportación / DUA (customs export declaration; for digital services, DGI export-of-services notification)
Bill of Lading or Airway Bill (physical goods movement; for digital services, retained network/server evidence of foreign consumption)
Inward Remittance Certificate / SWIFT MT103 or platform payout statement from AdMob/AppLovin payment rails
Export service contract with the foreign counterparty and proof that the service is used or consumed outside Panama
ITBMS refund application (Solicitud de Devolución) attaching zero-rated e-invoices and purchase invoices supporting input credits
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: DGI may claw back zero-rated ITBMS claimed without full substantiation within the 5-year statute of limitations, adding a 10% monthly surcharge (recargo) up to 100% of the tax, plus fines from PAB 500 to PAB 50,000 under Ley 8 de 2010; intentional evasion triggers criminal penalties under the Código Fiscal and removal from the export facilitation registry; failure to repatriate export proceeds within 180 days suspends future export benefits and may attract customs penalties.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Superintendencia de Bancos de Panama (SBP) - Superintendency of Banks of Panama; there is no statutory central bank. Banco Nacional de Panama acts as fiscal agency and settlement banker, while the Ministry of Economy and Finance executes monetary policy under a fully dollarized regime with the US Dollar as legal tender since 1904.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Full convertibility applies to both current and capital account transactions. The Panamanian Balboa (PAB) is a non-circulating unit of account pegged 1:1 to USD. Profit remittances, Private Interest Foundation distributions, founder disbursements, dividends, and capital repatriation require no exchange-control license, prior central bank approval, or tax clearance certificate. The only frictions are bank-level AML documentation under Ley 23 de 2015 and Ley 254 de 2021, plus UAF reporting; no quantitative limits, queues, or convertibility hurdles exist for ad-tech revenue collected from AdMob and AppLovin.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Not applicable. Panama imposes no statutory surrender timeline, mandatory conversion ratio, or repatriation channel for export receipts. Revenues from exported digital services under ISIC 5820 hyper-casual game publishing may be retained in USD indefinitely. The only implied obligation is traceability of receipts through an SBP-licensed institution and compliance with UAF suspicious transaction reporting.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Banco Nacional de Panama (State-owned fiscal agency)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: MEDIUM-LOW. Panama has no domestic digital-EMI licensing regime; foreign EMIs lack SBP regulatory standing and are not part of the national clearing system. Payoneer is operationally viable as a settlement conduit for AdMob and AppLovin marketplace payouts but should not serve as the primary liquidity rail. Wise Business lists Panama as a covered market but routinely declines Private Interest Foundations during due diligence. Mercury and Airwallex are legally unavailable to a Panama PIF without a US or EU corporate wrapper. Legal exposure also arises because EMI commingled segregation pools do not provide the deposit-protection privileges of a Panamanian bank. Recommended architecture: a local SBP-licensed bank account as the single collecting account, with any EMI used only as a receipt-boarding wallet before a weekly sweep to the bank.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: A physical or represented appearance is effectively mandatory for PIFs. SBP customer due diligence rules (SBP Acuerdo 1 de 2012 and subsequent guidance) require identity verification of the settlor, council members, protector where appointed, all signatories, and final beneficiaries. Banco General and Banistmo demand an in-branch biometric interview for the first signatory. Remote opening is available on a discretionary risk-based basis at Towerbank and Global Bank through a Zoom interview, apostilled foundation deed, legalised passport, and bank reference. Alternatively, a Panamanian resident lawyer holding an authenticated power of attorney may complete the interview in lieu of the foreign council member. Onboarding should be planned for 6 to 10 weeks; expectations improved materially after Panama was removed from the FATF grey list in October 2023.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Foundation privacy under Ley 21 de 2017: nominee or anonymous council membership and an undisclosed beneficiary schedule at account opening, so the bank cannot identify the Ultimate Beneficial Owner
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified copy of the Foundation Charter (Pacto Fundacional); certified act appointing the Foundation Council; signed beneficial-ownership schedule matching the UAF register under Ley 254 de 2021 (Certificado de Beneficiario Final); passport and personal bank reference of each UBO; waiver of statutory confidentiality executed in favour of the SBP bank.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inbound concentration risk: repeated high-value USD credits from Google AdMob and AppLovin without formal agreements or with a foreign payment aggregator interposed
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed Google AdMob publisher agreement and AppLovin publisher agreement naming the PIF as contractual counterparty; six-month payout history with dashboard screenshots; ad-network tax certification (W-9 or W-8BEN); written explanation of the contract flow showing the PIF as the receiving entity.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Pass-through or funnel pattern: funds moved out within 24 to 48 hours of receipt to developer pool accounts or contractor wallets, indicating possible unlicensed money transmission
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Treasury resolution establishing a 30-day liquidity buffer and a weekly disbursement calendar; signed contractor and developer agreements with fee milestones; itemized invoices and work-package evidence (SDK builds, user-acquisition campaign invoices); annual audited or reviewed financial statements of the PIF.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Jurisdiction and OFAC ambiguity: user traffic or ad mediation originates partially in sanctioned or high-risk jurisdictions, or payment references mention crypto-asset settlement
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Ad network geo-targeting report demonstrating exclusion of OFAC-sanctioned territories; GDPR and COPPA compliance certificates; written AML and sanctions policy manual of the foundation; sworn declaration that no crypto-assets are received or settled.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Undisclosed founder wealth: substantial initial foundation endowment above USD 100,000 without documentation of the founder's source of wealth
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarised source-of-wealth statement of the founder; audited accounts or tax returns of the founder's prior company; sale or funding agreements of the previous gaming studio; bank reference from the remitting institution; legal opinion confirming the endowment's compliance with Ley 21 de 2017.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Capital injections are routed via SWIFT MT103 from the founder's bank to the PIF account at the selected SBP bank with payment reference DOTACION FUNDACIONAL and the foundation registration number; no balance-of-payments approval is required. The remitting bank must evidence the founder's source of wealth; the receiving bank verifies the PIF's certificate of existence, council incumbency, and UAF beneficial-ownership filing. Ad revenue from AdMob and AppLovin arrives as standard SWIFT MT103 wire payments referencing the publisher ID. No mandatory purpose codes exist under Panamanian regulation, but the bank's AML questionnaire requires the commercial description ADVERTISING REVENUE - HYPER-CASUAL GAMES and the underlying agreement. Funds clear in USD via Fedwire and CHIPS through the bank's New York correspondent with same-day finality.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Operating costs for developers, user-acquisition vendors, cloud infrastructure, and staff are settled by SWIFT MT103 direct payments in USD; where an intermediary bank requires a correspondent leg, MT202 COVER is used. Commercial letters of credit and documentary collections are not standard for digital service trade and are not recommended given cost and documentation burden. Domestic supplier payments can be cleared through ACH Panama operated under SBP oversight. Every outbound payment must be supported by a contract or invoice retained in the foundation's treasury file. Virtual-IBAN solutions are permissible only when issued by a licensed Panamanian bank holding the underlying funds; foreign EMI virtual accounts are neither recognized nor recommended as clearing rails.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: USD/EUR deliverable over-the-counter forward contract with an SBP-licensed bank, hedging EUR-denominated AdMob settlements
USD/GBP deliverable forward contract for GBP-denominated affiliate or advertising settlements
Cross-currency basis swap (USD against EUR or GBP) for quarterly aggregate balances above USD 5 million
Plain vanilla FX option (USD call / EUR put) at licensed commercial banks; no hedge attestation or derivative filing is required under Panamanian law
No NDF market exists or is needed because USD is full legal tender in Panama; PAB is a non-circulating currency pegged 1:1, making deliverable USD hedges redundant

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Private Interest Foundation fee / flat annual government fee (franchise-tax equivalent)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI), Ministry of Economy and Finance, Panama; standing is reflected in the Registro Público de Panamá
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Due annually no later than 31 January for each calendar year; public-registry good standing is assessed from the date the DGI records payment
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: 10% late-payment surcharge plus default interest under the Fiscal Code; continued non-payment for the applicable consecutive annual periods permits the Registro Público to administratively strike off the foundation and cancel its legal personality.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25% standard Panamanian corporate income tax (Impuesto sobre la Renta) on net Panama-source taxable income, payable in USD/Balboa at parity.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Territorial taxation: income from foreign sources, including AdMob and AppLovin ad-monetization payouts for hyper-casual mobile games played and serviced outside Panama, is excluded from Panamanian taxable income. Preferential regimes include the Multinational Headquarters (SEM) program at effective 0%–5% rates on qualifying international services and certain trading activities; a compliant Private Interest Foundation (PIF) earning exclusively foreign-source publishing revenue carries a projected Panamanian effective corporate income tax rate of 0% on that stream.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Formulario 249 (Declaracion Jurada de Impuestos sobre la Renta para Personas Juridicas / Annual Corporate Income Tax Return) filed exclusively through the DGI's electronic platform Sistema T@T (dgi.tat.pa), authenticated with the entity's RUC and digital certificate.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual (Form 249) with quarterly advance income tax payments (pagos de anticipo) due within each quarter for the current fiscal period and final reconciliation performed in the annual return.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within the fourth month after the close of the fiscal year; for calendar-year filers the statutory deadline is no later than April 30 of the succeeding year. The PIF may adopt a non-calendar fiscal year only with prior DGI authorization.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 1 / Ingresos brutos obtenidos en Panama
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross income derived from activities performed, goods situated, or services rendered in Panamanian territory under Código Fiscal Article 2 territorial-source rule.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter zero where all hyper-casual ad revenue arises from AdMob/AppLovin contracts negotiated, executed and performed outside Panama; attach a territorial-source analysis naming the foreign operators and servers used for ad mediation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 2 / Ingresos exentos o rentas de fuente extranjera
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Foreign-source receipts and exempt income reported separately to create a verifiable audit trail of the territorial exemption.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Disclose aggregate foreign ad-monetization proceeds and identify counterparties (e.g., Google Ireland Ltd., AppLovin Corp.) in the attachment; never net foreign expenses against Panama-source income lines.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Costs and expenses incurred to generate Panama-source income, including applicable local salaries, depreciation and allocable overhead.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Restrict deductions to costs supporting Panama-source activities; maintain an objective cost-allocation ratio (e.g., revenue share) for group-wide service costs and retain transfer-pricing documentation supporting the split.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net operating loss claimed for carryforward against future taxable income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Only losses generated by Panama-source activities qualify; apply the 5-year carryforward limit under the Código Fiscal and attach a computation showing the originating fiscal year.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Anexo Precios de Transferencia (Transfer Pricing Annex)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Sworn disclosure of related-party cross-border transactions, selected arm's-length method and comparability summary.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Mandatory when annual related-party cross-border transactions exceed B/. 1,000,000; for smaller flows, state N/A but preserve contemporaneous analyses supporting the app-store revenue split and IP returns.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Ultimate beneficial owner declaration aligned with Law 23 of 2015 and the foundation's internal registry maintained by the resident agent.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a PIF, identify the founder, council members and any natural-person beneficiary in the economic chain; provide passport or entity identification data. The registry remains non-public but is accessible to DGI, UAF and foreign tax authorities under exchange-of-information.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing of Form 249 exposes the entity to a fine of up to B/. 250, a monthly surcharge of 1% of the tax due for each month or fraction of delay, and default interest at the DGI's official daily rate (approximately 0.0329% per day). Non-payment of assessed tax may trigger asset embargoes, suspension of RUC and commercial registration, and criminal referral where evasion is evidenced; continued failure to file for three consecutive years creates a rebuttable presumption of fraudulent intent with exposure to the evasion penalties.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 10% complementary dividend withholding tax on distributions made from profits previously subject to Panamanian corporate income tax (aggregate burden approximating 32.5% pre-credits); 20% on distributions made from profits not previously subject to Panamanian corporate tax (e.g., untaxed Panama-source earnings); 0% on distributions sourced entirely from foreign-source income under the territorial principle when documented, and 0% for qualifying dividend distribution under SEM regime conditions.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Panama has in-force comprehensive double taxation agreements including Spain, Mexico, South Korea, Singapore, Luxembourg and Barbados, generally reducing the 10%/20% complementary dividend tax to 5%–10% for treaty-resident beneficial owners. Protocol: (1) obtain an official Certificate of Fiscal Residence (TRC / Certificado de Residencia Fiscal) issued by the foreign tax authority; (2) complete the DGI-recognized beneficial owner claim form and substantiate that treaty substance criteria are met; (3) provide the TRC and ownership chain documentation to the Panamanian payer before distribution; where WHT was over-deducted, file a refund claim within the statutory prescriptive period (generally five years under the Código Fiscal); (4) archive the TRC and shareholding evidence for at least seven years. Caution: no comprehensive income tax treaty exists with the United States; US-origin royalty or ad-servicing payments to the PIF remain exposed to US statutory 30% withholding absent a specific exemption.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Panama-source royalties paid to non-residents: statutory withholding of 12.5%, treaty-reduced normally to 10% (e.g., Spain, Korea, Singapore, Mexico). Panama-source interest paid to non-residents: statutory 12.5%, treaty-reduced to 5%–10% under most in-force DTAs, with certain export/import finance interest statutorily exempt. Outbound hyper-casual flows: payments from AdMob/AppLovin to the PIF are foreign-source and attract no Panamanian WHT, but the contracts may carry Irish or US source-country withholding where the consideration contains license-of-IP elements (Irish withholding ordinarily mitigable under EU instruments; US withholding 30% absent treaty).

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: B/. 1,000,000 (USD 1,000,000 at Balboa parity) of aggregate annual cross-border related-party transactions triggers the mandatory Local File annexed to Form 249 via Sistema T@T. A Master File is required where the multinational group's consolidated worldwide gross revenue equals or exceeds B/. 100,000,000. Irrespective of threshold, the PIF must retain contemporaneous transfer-pricing documentation covering the hyper-casual ad-monetization model: app-store revenue attribution, ad mediation economics, IP ownership and risk assumption, and intercompany royalty-setting.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Executive Decree 198 of 2020, implementing Law 70 of 2019 and FATF/OECD ESR standards, applies to Panamanian resident entities earning relevant income, expressly including income from intellectual property assets, licensing, financing, distribution and agency services. Obligations include performing core income-generating activities in Panama (local management decisions, qualified personnel, physical premises, proportionate operating expenditure) and filing the annual ESR declaration through the designated system with the resident agent within the statutory window following fiscal year-end. For an ISIC 5820 hyper-casual publisher, active foreign publishing may fall outside the listed relevant activities, but a structure where the PIF licenses game IP to foreign operators will attract ESR scrutiny. Failure to satisfy ESR results in administrative penalties, non-renewal of the resident agent's license, cancellation of the PIF's registration, and adverse information exchange under EOIR/transparency mechanisms.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Falsely labeling Panama-source ad-monetization revenue as foreign-source; filing a materially false Form 249; backdating or fabricating outsourcing contracts with AdMob/AppLovin affiliates or intermediary shell entities to shift or eliminate Panamanian tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Fines of 2 to 5 times the tax evaded (Código Fiscal Articles 710–711), plus the full unpaid tax, default interest and a surcharge up to 50% of the tax; criminal conviction for fiscal evasion carries imprisonment of 2 to 5 years and disqualification from operating commercial entities in Panama.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors, founder and council members who sign or approve fraudulent returns are jointly and severally liable for the tax debt; Panamanian courts may pierce the foundation's separate personality (levantamiento del velo) upon proof of fraud or abuse; criminal proceedings authorize travel bans, asset freezes, and final imprisonment of responsible natural persons.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Use of the PIF to layer ad-payout funds of unknown or illicit provenance; failure of the resident agent, founder or beneficiaries to disclose the ultimate beneficial owner; commingling of personal funds with foundation revenue through nominee-arranged accounts; executing factually baseless circular loans among related entities.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative fines imposed by the Unidad de Analisis Financiero (UAF) of up to B/. 1,000,000 per violation; cancellation of the foundation's registration and the resident agent's license; criminal prosecution under Penal Code Article 390 for money laundering with imprisonment of 5 to 12 years and asset confiscation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Natural-person founders and directors face criminal indictment with passport surrender, travel bans, freezing of personal accounts and up to 12 years of imprisonment; civil restitution claims lie for affected parties; the corporate veil is pierced where the foundation was established for concealment or fraud.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Economic Substance Failure (ESR and EOIR)
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Claiming territorial exemption and treaty benefits through a PIF possessing zero local substance: no office, employees, or local management; administrative-only representation via the resident agent; no ESR or beneficial-ownership returns filed; continuous material IP/ad-monetization income retained with negligible economic activity in Panama.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: ESR administrative penalties per Executive Decree 198 of 2020; cancellation of the PIF charter for continued non-compliance; DGI may disregard the entity and recharacterize revenues as Panama-source based on exchange-of-information disclosures; adverse international listings and consequential termination of bank accounts are realistic collateral consequences.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Managers maintaining fictitious substance are personally liable for restored taxes and fines; courts may impose civil restitution orders, travel bans during investigation, and criminal fraud liability (imprisonment up to 5 years) for deliberately false ESR declarations.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Withholding and Distribution Non-Compliance (Dividends / Founder Payments)
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Distributing dividends, interim or founder payments, or advances to beneficiaries without withholding the 10%/20% complementary dividend tax; recharacterizing distributions as shareholder loans with no arm's-length interest or repayment schedule; failing to file the annual shareholder distribution and dividend information declarations with DGI.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The PIF bears solidary liability for the unpaid WHT, fines up to 100% of the withheld amount, default interest and monthly surcharges; DGI may reclassify nominal loans as constructive dividends subject to assessment at the 20% top-up rate and deny all related deductions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors approving non-compliant distributions are jointly and severally liable for the WHT deficiency and penalties; distributions made during insolvency are clawed back; criminal referral for breach of withholding-agent duties can generate travel bans and imprisonment of up to 4 years for the responsible persons.
